title: Brent Kochuba Says the Real Tech Top Wasn't the News Everyone Blamed
speaker: Brent Kochuba (SpotGamma), with Kevin Davitt (Nasdaq)

macro_themes.view: Money is rotating from tech into equal-weight/laggards (RSP, Nike); a broadening rally is a bullish construct, a mild correction not a bear market.
SMH and Korea topped Oct 6 on Chinese memory maker CXMT news, not on the Anthropic headlines blamed later.
Bigger risk into year-end is missing an upside move; fixed-strike vols and NDX skews near lows show no panic.
10-year off from 5.3% to 5.1% supports rate-sensitive beaten-down names.

calls.condition: Bullish unless SPX loses 7,700 or 1-month correlation spikes, which would signal a broad-based sell-off.
calls.reason: Monthly OPEX clearing puts could mark a short-term low; fixed-strike vols falling; positive seasonality into year-end.
calls.quote: if we start to lose 7,700 in the S&P 500 then I'm going to start worrying about a more of a broad-based sell-off.

calls.reason: Single-stock OPEX in mega-cap tech should relieve put pressure for a short-term low; NDX December skews near 90-day lows, no panic bid; tech more volatile both ways.
calls.quote: I do think we could put in at least a a short-term low here with expiration as put options are cleared out

calls.reason: After a 15% drop from the Oct 6 top, SMH is cheaper to get into; wants upside right-tail options as a core holding.
calls.quote: SMH I think now is a lot cheaper and easier to get into some trades there.

calls.reason: NVDA calls are cheap; holding upside calls to avoid missing a right-tail move.
calls.quote: I want to maintain exposure with the talk about Nvidia calls for example how cheap they are.

notes: Friday monthly OPEX morning; dated 2026-10-16. Nike, NBIS, TSLA call buying mentioned as flows only - not recorded as calls. Kevin Davitt gave no directional calls.
